headline: New York City's public schools, the largest school system in the United States, have banned generative AI for students from the youngest grades through eighth grade for the 2026-27 school year.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the policy was announced on 2 Sep 2026 (ABC's article is dated 2 Sep; Google News showed it as 17 Oct), and no new development was found.
importance_line: More than half a million students and their teachers lose student-facing AI tools this school year and software makers lose a large customer for them, while the city calls the ban a one-year pause to study the effects, not a final verdict on AI in classrooms.
summary: ABC News reports that the New York City school district, the largest in the United States, confirmed a one-year ban on student-facing generative AI (software that writes text or makes images for students) for more than half a million students from the 2-K early-years program through eighth grade, and a ban on companion chatbots. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani says the city will spend the year studying the technology's effects, high school students are not covered, and the policy was announced on 2 Sep 2026, so this is a follow-up to early-September coverage.
notes: Read in full on ABC News. ABC's page metadata gives 2 Sep 2026 as publication date; Google News listed it as 17 Oct 2026 (re-dated), so this is old news, not a new decision. Cross-checked with the NYC.gov press release of 2 Sep 2026 (nearly 600,000 students; ban covers 2-K to 8th grade; companion chatbots banned in all grades; five limited high school pilots). Suggest the main session treats it as NO OLD NEWS unless it finds a real new development.
